scope: Four selected occupations linked qualitatively to existing market-stage cells; not a national physical-labor or robot-addressability estimate.

evidence.claim: The 2025 ORS source is preliminary third-wave evidence from two samples collected August 2023 through July 2025; it is not a time series of robot capability or physical-work change.
evidence.observation_period: 2025 preliminary reference year; samples August 2023 through July 2025
evidence.locator: File information!A1:B1; Footnote codes P; ORS 2025 dataset
evidence.limitations: Preliminary aggregate, not a single-date census. No comparisons across ORS waves are treated as a trend.

evidence.claim: Published mean workday standing shares are 97.7% for janitors, 89.2% for construction laborers, 95.6% for team assemblers and 93.7% for hand material movers. Team assemblers' mean sitting row is absent from this workbook.
evidence.observation_period: 2025 preliminary reference year; samples August 2023 through July 2025
evidence.locator: ORS 2025 dataset, estimate codes 01003 and 00997; exact rows in selected_rows.json
evidence.limitations: Standing includes walking; sitting includes lying down. These duration measures are not the share of work a robot can perform. The missing sitting estimate is not filled as 100 minus standing.

evidence.claim: The four occupations have distinct published manipulation, reaching and low-posture requirements; the selected team-assembler reaching rows are absent. Incidence measures describe workers with a requirement, not the fraction of their hours spent on it.
evidence.observation_period: 2025 preliminary reference year; samples August 2023 through July 2025
evidence.locator: ORS 2025 dataset, estimate codes 00771, 01262, 00830, 00831 and 01216; exact source rows retained
evidence.limitations: Requirements can overlap in a worker and time interval. No marginal percentages are added or multiplied into joint prevalence or employment.

evidence.claim: OEWS detailed codes match janitors, construction laborers and hand material movers, with 2,209,760, 1,096,780 and 2,950,280 jobs respectively. No exact Team Assemblers 51-2092 row exists. The broader 51-2090 category appears as both broad and detailed rows with the same 1,405,030 jobs.
evidence.observation_period: May 2025; six panels November 2022 through May 2025
evidence.locator: national_M2025_dl rows 720, 988, 1163, 1164 and 1389; AREA=99, NAICS=000000, OWN_CODE=1235
evidence.limitations: The two 51-2090 rows are classification aliases, not additive employment. Their total is not assigned to Team Assemblers. Matching codes still do not align survey populations.

evidence.claim: ORS civilian workers exclude federal, military, agricultural, private-household and self-employed workers. OEWS covers nonfarm wage-and-salary jobs including federal executive/Postal employment and selected agricultural industries. The same SOC code does not by itself make these populations interchangeable.
evidence.locator: ORS profiles: General terms, civilian workers; OEWS technical note: Scope, industry coding and concepts
evidence.limitations: No employment times ORS incidence or workday percentage calculation is permitted without a reconciled population and duration design.
evidence.publication_date_missing_reason: Live methods page does not expose a verified publication date; definitions are explicitly labeled for the 2025 data.

evidence.claim: ORS source dashes carry different meanings: footnote 6 means standard error below 0.5, while footnote 15 means unavailable. Estimate ranges such as >99.5 and >95 are not point values; the two range types have different construction rules.
evidence.observation_period: 2025 preliminary reference year; samples August 2023 through July 2025
evidence.locator: Footnote codes!A2:B35; range-estimates methodology; selected row footnote columns
evidence.limitations: The >99.5/<0.5 endpoint ranges do not incorporate a confidence interval; other published ranges use the BLS one-sided interval method. Bounds are retained, not replaced with endpoints or midpoint assumptions.

evidence.claim: ORS gross and fine manipulation can occur concurrently; fine manipulation in the third wave includes keyboarding. These requirements therefore cannot serve as a clean measure of economically substitutable physical labor.
evidence.limitations: Requires task/workflow, tooling, quality, supervision and useful-output evidence before a robot comparison. No standalone dexterity score or annual-hour conversion follows.
evidence.publication_date_missing_reason: Live methods page does not expose a verified publication date; definitions are explicitly labeled for the 2025 data.
